text: {"status":"contradicted","evidence_ids":["ev-ce41690aa36014fdb717d1b4"],"request_dft":false,"proposed_test_ids":[],"rationale":"The claim is that the archived ideal olivine LiFePO4 calculation represents AFM ordering, with net cell moment at or below 0.5 muB. The converged DFT relaxation record (VASP PBE, ionic accuracy reached, force 0.0096 eV/A below the 0.01 threshold) reports total_magnetization_abs = 16.0 muB for the Li4Fe4P4O16 cell. That is far above the 0.5 threshold. It is also exactly 4 Fe x 4 muB, the ferromagnetic high-spin Fe2+ value. The initial magmom was all-parallel (Fe 5.0 muB), so the archived calculation was started as FM and stayed FM. It does not represent AFM ordering. The record is admissible (measured, converged_dft), and it covers the stated target structure. No other records disagree, so there is no conflict. The evidence decides the claim as stated, which concerns what the archived calculation represents, and the answer is contradicted. A new AFM-versus-FM comparison would be useful for finding the true ground state, but it would not change the verdict on this archived calculation. I therefore do not request DFT or the follow-up test. No peers have spoken, so I have no peer claims to support or dispute yet. My assumption is that total_magnetization_abs is the cell net moment and not a sum of absolute site moments. If it were the latter, 16 muB would be consistent with AFM. The all-parallel initialization makes the net-moment reading more likely. A falsification check is to inspect the per-site moments in the OUTCAR, where AFM would show alternating signs."}
